looks like behavior of the API for List with a non-0 resourceVersion differs when the watch cache is enabled and when it is disabled.

with the watch cache enabled, the API has the "at least as new as" behavior, as best as I can tell

with the watch cache disabled:
* successful responses return the List as it existed at that resourceVersion (resources are returned as they existed at that version, newer resources are not included)
* if the requested version has already been compacted, you get 410 errors:
```
$ curl -k https://localhost:6443/api/v1/configmaps?resourceVersion=1
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {
    
  },
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "The resourceVersion for the provided list is too old.",
  "reason": "Expired",
  "code": 410
}
```

we cannot switch clients to using an API with behavior that unstable

comment_text: Are we sure this isn't reintroducing the issue fixed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/49992 ?

> It looks to me like Jordan Liggitt has pointed out a inconsistency between cache enabled vs cache disabled that we should deal with separately, but that doesn't prevent us from making this particular fix, or am I missing something?

It makes clients and controllers start using the list API in a new way they did not previously use. That new call pattern does not have consistent behavior, and is not well tested. We know it returns errors the lister/watchers do not handle properly (410 errors on relist requests). We should not change clients/controllers/reflectors to use this API in this way until these issues are resolved.

In general, I'm not in favor of modifying the etcd implementations to match the cacher implementation... I think the burden is on the cacher to match native semantics.

I also am hesitant to start changing implemented behavior before settling on an approach that will also address the component restart issue.

The fun question is when it is safe to switch clients to this behavior. If we change reflectors globally, one built using the new code can get 410 responses running against an n-1 server on a resource with watch cache off, and never list successfully again. We may need to handle 410 responses on list specifically for this reason.

If a reflector re-listing with rv=n gets a 410 response, I think we should fall back to list without rv.

The only path I know of where a list can return a 410 today is when the watch cache is disabled. In that case, listing without rv gets latest content and is safe against time travel.

If the watch cache was somehow enabled and returned a 410, listing without rv still goes to etcd and is safe against time travel.

if so, that doesn't match how we handle wildcard prefix normalization in getAllowlistImagePattern... that means an allowlist entry of `foo/*` would currently allow `foo/bar` or `foo/bar:baz` or `foo/bar@sha256:...` but with this normalization would not (because ParseNormalizedNamed would insert `docker.io/`)

add unit tests to cover library-less and host-less allowlist entries, and either continue using `image` for prefix checks (likely) or switch `getAllowlistImagePattern` to construct prefix matches using the same normalization (if that's even possible... I'm not sure it is)
I don't think we should log here... the image is user input and is not required to pass this parsing in API validation
if we can't parse this, we should still check `image` against `prefixes`

Kubernetes explicitly avoids adding in host / library segments in API server and kubelet to pass the image down to CRI unmodified, only possibly adding in a default tag:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4a1ca6c68ed8b1bf17423b670d7b6ccc8185b2f9/pkg/kubelet/images/image_manager.go#L424-L429

> We _probably_ should use the image that actually gets pulled when writing the record?

Yeah, I really thought we were using that verbatim
seems like we should *really* understand why this increased in frequency significantly 5 days ago before we suppress it

/lgtm
/approve
/skip

there's a working theory (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135713#issuecomment-4092666900) that when the stop races with the actual underlying `runc create`, an exit code of 2 can result

the PLEGOnDemand feature makes the kubelet react instantly to delete requests instead of coalescing them on a 2 second poll boundary, so makes a fast create-then-delete much more likely to translate into a race between runc creating and stopping the container

once we prove this is what is happening, tolerating a slightly different non-zero exit here seems ~ok to me (even if we want to pursue improving containerd / runc to produce a more consistent error code in that scenario)

it's looking more and more like runc handling of the term signal prior to handoff to the underlying process is the cause of the 2 exit code, I think this PR to add that to the list of non-zero exit codes we accept is fine.

Maybe also limit this to the `t.Message == ""` case? If some other non-empty message shows up that doesn't match this pattern, we don't want to ignore it

```suggestion
		case t.ExitCode == 2 && t.Reason == "Error" && t.Message == "":
```
let's also log that this is happening (similar to the reBug88766 logging below), and point to a specific runc issue with details

/lgtm
/approve
